abstract: We describe multimode solitons made of purely spatial modes using the mathematical formalism developed for the elliptical polarization soliton, and we extend this formalism to solitons made of more than two modes. The main difference with the polarization mode case is the asymmetry in the nonlinear coefficients. Strictly speaking, these objects are solitary waves, whose modal temporal profiles remain invariant owing to the incoherent nonlinear interaction between modes. The approach consists of finding the trajectories of a unit-mass ball in an analogous potential, which correspond to stationary solutions of our set of nonlinear coupled equations. Our analysis reveals a rich variety of multimode solitons with more complex temporal profiles, so-called multihumped multimode solitons. These are new and highly complex nonlinear objects. While fundamental multimode solitons are stable against noise and symmetry breaking, the stability of multihumped multimode solitons depends on their position in the parameter space. The fission of multihumped solitons yields several less complex multihumped solitons, together with fundamental multimode solitons. For the latter, Raman nonlinearity can induce a net energy transfer between modes with different group velocities, whereas self-steepening only modifies the overall velocity of the solitary wave.
